title: Elks, the Bulls night parades and Claiborne neutral ground
summary: He ties the Bulls to the Elks and describes the night parades with a live bull, and the Claiborne Avenue neutral ground where he lived.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: The Elks must have built that house. Yeah, well the Elks took the bulls over. Now speaking about that, because you see the Elks, they first, when I joined the Elks, it was on a street called, on Drysdale, Melpomene, used to be the old Mason Hall. Yeah, I believe I was sworn in the Elks in 1935, during the WPA, URA band time, that's when I was a man in Elk, and of course I stood in a good while and just dropped right on out like that. But during them areas and that, I'll bring it back to the bulls' time. Now, speaking about the night parades, now where two places I feel they could get the bulls from, they used in their night parades to be in their truck, they had one large bull, they had to get two places, they could be called the Crescent City Slaughterhouse, that's way down in the night ward, and they'll have a live hour bull, and they'll have, each side of his home they'll have a rope tied around it, to the wing of the truck, I mean the sides of the truck, and he'd come along in the middle of the parade when they, they're making, en route like that. At night? That's right, at night, and they had what you call these little flambeau lights, you know, and all the men have that, and they have their fun like that. And I was there at that time living on the street they called Seminard between Vera and Robison.

The big wide street, yeah. They hadn't paved it then, during them days it used to be like these bricks-like, something just like North Peter Street is. You see, that's what you call the Tor blocks. But during them Seminard Avenue had them little bricks. Well, the parade would come down, far as Claiborne, I imagine they'd go to the Frenchman Street, make a ton, and come up Claiborne, and where'd they go from there, I wouldn't know. But that's how we all would call it the circle during them days, you see, because that you had the old North Claiborne Street car used to run through there, and we had, in the middle of the neutral ground they had a paving. People used to walk through there at night, the summer nights, meet girls and their friends, and they'd by just walk up and down. Some people in the evening time, cheering, skating. Yeah, like a little park. Yeah, but it used to run all together from Canal and Claiborne, clean on down to Elision Field Avenue, that neutral ground did, and the street calls on each side, in the neutral ground running, and they didn't have much traffic like you got now, you see. And then as far as when you leave Claiborne and Canal, it'd run a piece, and then we had, near Tulane there we had the Claiborne Market there, it used to block you off.
Is that near where the Circle Market is now?
Yeah, where the Circle was at now, that used to be nothing but houses there.
Yeah, you see the market used, I mean the Seminar Market was right there, but it wasn't that kind of building, it was built like on the old side, something like the French Market.
Oh I see, so the Circle Market is pretty near.
